incidents.name: Apollo 1
incidents.text: During a launch pad test, a flash fire broke out in the sealed cabin, filled with pure oxygen. All three astronauts died.
incidents.quote: Because of the pure oxygen atmosphere, pressurized to 16.7 psi – two pounds above atmospheric pressure and a larger-than-allowable amount of flammable material in the spacecraft – the fire spread very rapidly.
incidents.sourceTitle: NASA History: 55 Years Ago: The Apollo 1 Fire and its Aftermath
support: At 6:31 p.m., a flash fire broke out inside the cabin.
By the time they opened the hatches, the crew had already perished.

incidents.name: Apollo 13
incidents.text: On the way to the Moon, an oxygen tank with likely damaged wiring insulation shorted, a spark set off combustion inside the tank, and the tank burst. The crew made it home.
incidents.quote: They had stirred the oxygen tanks on two previous occasions during the mission with only erratic pressure readings, but this time, likely due to the damaged Teflon insulation, a short-circuit occurred triggering a spark resulting in a combustion event.
incidents.sourceTitle: NASA History: 50 Years Ago: Apollo 13 Review Board Report
support: The pressure tank lost integrity and the oxygen escaping at high velocity caused the panel covering bay 4 to be blown off.
while traveling 205,000 miles from Earth toward the Moon, an explosion rocked the Apollo 13 spacecraft
successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 17

incidents.name: Mir
incidents.text: An oxygen generator caught fire, blocked the way to an escape craft and filled the station with smoke. The crew put it out, with no lasting harm.
incidents.quote: On Feb. 24, 1997, the six crew members aboard the Russian space station Mir faced significant danger when a fire ignited in an oxygen generating system.
incidents.sourceTitle: NASA History: 25 Years Ago: Fire Aboard Space Station Mir
support: The searing flame, lasting several minutes, not only cut off access to one of the two Soyuz escape vehicles but also filled the station’s modules with smoke.
the crew prevailed and extinguished the flames
with no lasting harm to the crew members
